newsitem.title: USA: CompuCom expects Q2 sales to exceed Q1's.
newsitem.headline: CompuCom expects Q2 sales to exceed Q1's.

text.p: CompuCom Systems Inc said Wednesday it expects its second quarter 1997 sales to exceed the level achieved in the first quarter, saying there is a continued demand by corporate customers for desktop products.
"We expect sequential quarterly improvement in product sales for the second quarter," said Ed Anderson, president and chief executive officer of the company.
Anderson made the remark as CompuCom reported the total revenue of the company for the first quarter rose to $431.9 million from $413.3 million in the quarter a year ago.
"The service business continued to be strong, up 63 percent from the same period a year ago, in spite of flat product growth," he said.
There is a "strong indication" there has been continued demand by corporate customers for asset management of the distributed desktop, he added.

CompuCom, a reseller of personal computer products and provider of network integration services, took steps during the fourth quarter of 1996 to reduce inventory levels and implement cost-cutting programs.

The company is now pleased with the results as first quarter operating expenses declined $4.4 million from the fourth quarter, while inventory levels fell approximately $40 million when, compared with both March 31, 1996 and December 31, 1996, he said.
